transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-21
Start: 16:00 PDT
Duration: ~57 minutes
Attendees: Jamie Park (Redwood AE), Ravi Singh (Redwood SE), Maya Torres (CISO, Veridian), Ethan Cole (Platform Lead), Dr. Sarah Nguyen (Head of Data), Liam Brooks (Security Engineer)

Summary:
Quick security posture discovery focused on hosted vs dedicated vs private deployment options. Veridian is evaluating moving PHI workloads to an LLM-backed assistant for clinicians; primary concerns: SOC 2/ISO compliance, SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs, encryption and KMS, data residency and retention. AE+SE explained Redwood's controls, Dedicated/Private tradeoffs, and requested docs and a technical deep dive.

Topics Covered:
- Compliance posture: SOC2 Type II, ISO 27001
- Authentication and SSO: SAML/SCIM, IdP integrations (Okta, Azure AD)
- Authorization: RBAC, token management, least privilege
- Audit logging and data access logs
- Encryption at rest and in transit, KMS/HSM options
- Data retention policies, data residency and deletion guarantees
- Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private: tradeoffs for PHI and regulatory requirements
- Rollout and pilot: benching perf, cost vs latency, fallback plans

Transcript body:
[00:00] Jamie Park: Hi everyone thanks for joining, um I'm Jamie from Redwood, AE on the account, and with me is Ravi who's our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
[00:08] Maya Torres: Good thanks, Maya here, CISO at Veridian. Appreciate you fitting us in. We try to get alignment on security controls before a pilot.
[00:15] Ravi Singh: Great, thanks Maya. Quick agenda - we want to understand your current stack, compliance needs, and specific must-haves so we can recommend hosted, dedicated, or private.
[00:25] Ethan Cole: Sounds good. Quick context - we're building a clinician assistant that surfaces patient notes. Some PHI will be in model inputs so we have to be careful about egress and retention.
[00:35] Dr. Sarah Nguyen: Also we want to keep latency sub-200ms p95 for short queries, but cost matters too.
[00:41] Jamie Park: Understood. First question - what's your current compliance posture and what attestation do you require?
[00:47] Maya Torres: We're SOC2 Type II right now, moving toward ISO 27001 next quarter. For any vendor handling PHI we need SOC2, encryption, and evidence of SSO integration, plus vendor access logs.
[00:59] Ravi Singh: Redwood is SOC 2 Type II compliant; we can share the report under NDA. We also have an ISO readiness pack and have customers on ISO programs - we can share the scope.
[01:12] Ethan Cole: Can you clarify what data is stored in the hosted model? Do you keep prompts or outputs?
[01:18] Jamie Park: For our hosted offering by default we retain logs and request traces for 30 days for debugging and moderation; customers can request data-retention configurations. For PHI workloads we generally recommend Dedicated or Private so you control retention and logs.
[01:32] Maya Torres: Ok that makes sense. What about encryption - KMS and HSM support?
[01:36] Ravi Singh: We support TLS in transit and AES-256 at rest. For Dedicated and Private we offer customer-owned KMS integrations - AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, and bring-your-own-HSM for Private deployments. For Hosted we use our managed KMS but can offer envelope encryption for additional controls.
[01:51] Liam Brooks: For HIPAA concerns, will we be able to rotate keys and revoke access quickly?
[01:55] Ravi Singh: Yes, key rotation and revoke are supported when you bring your KMS; for hosted we have key rotation policies and we can discuss SLAs for emergency key revocation with enterprise contracts.
[02:06] Maya Torres: Audit logs - we need immutable logs showing who accessed what, when, and what was returned. Is that available?
[02:13] Jamie Park: We provide audit logs for API calls, admin actions, and console events. On Dedicated/Private you get raw log access and can ship logs to your SIEM (Splunk, Sumo, Datadog). Hosted includes console audit views and export capabilities.
[02:27] Dr. Sarah Nguyen: How granular is RBAC? We want tenant-level separation inside our workspace and ability to restrict model rollouts to certain teams.
[02:33] Ravi Singh: RBAC is role-based with custom roles, per-route permissions, and model-level controls. You can restrict who can deploy model rollouts, set canary rules, or only allow certain models for production.
[02:44] Ethan Cole: SSO - we use Okta and some groups in Azure AD, need SCIM for provisioning.
[02:50] Jamie Park: We support SAML SSO and SCIM for user provisioning. Integration is standard with Okta/Azure. SE can share config steps and sample metadata.
[03:00] Liam Brooks: Any multi-tenant leakage risks with hosted? We don't want any possibility of KV cache or prefix cache leaking across customers.
[03:08] Ravi Singh: Great question. Our hosted runtime isolates KV caches per customer by default and we have strict namespace separation. For absolute separation and to meet HIPAA controls we usually recommend Dedicated or Private where the underlying infra is tenant-hosted.
[03:22] Maya Torres: If we go Dedicated, how much control do we have over network isolation - VPC peering, private links?
[03:28] Ravi Singh: Dedicated offers VPC peering, private connectivity, and can be single-tenant GPU pools. Private adds a customer-managed control plane for on-prem or VPC deployments. We'll include architecture diagrams.
[03:40] Ethan Cole: Does Redwood support bringing models that we've fine-tuned internally? We need to ensure weights don't leave our environment.
[03:47] Ravi Singh: You can bring your model to Dedicated or Private; in Private the weights never leave your network. In Dedicated, the model files can be stored in customer-controlled object storage with access controls. For hosted, we'd use our curated model catalog and fine-tuning would be managed with explicit agreements.
[04:03] Jamie Park: Let's talk retention policies and deletion. If Veridian requires a 7-day retention window and immediate purge on request, can that be enforced?
[04:12] Maya Torres: Yes we need data deletion support for test data and patient-identifiable info.
[04:16] Ravi Singh: For Dedicated and Private we can set retention to your SLA and implement deletion APIs to purge logs/inputs. For hosted, we have configurable retention windows; emergency purge may be possible but is slower due to multi-tenant architecture unless on contract.
[04:30] Liam Brooks: How are admin roles audited? Do you provide change history for RBAC policies?
[04:34] Jamie Park: Yes - admin changes, role grants, and policy updates are recorded in the audit trail with actor, timestamp, and before/after snapshots. Those are exportable.
[04:44] Dr. Sarah Nguyen: Wanted to raise question about model hallucination and safeguards - are there content filtering or redaction features that run before data is persisted?
[04:52] Ravi Singh: We have moderation hooks and can configure redaction for PII extraction on ingress before saving. That can be part of the pipeline for PHI-sensitive deployments.
[05:04] Ethan Cole: On SLA/uptime - dedicated vs hosted, what do you offer?
[05:08] Jamie Park: Hosted has a higher uptime SLA for general customers, but for enterprise Dedicated comes with tighter latency and throughput guarantees and SLA-backed latency p95 targets. Private can be negotiated in enterprise contracts.
[05:20] Maya Torres: On legal - do you sign BAAs for HIPAA covered data?
[05:24] Jamie Park: Redwood is willing to sign BAAs for Dedicated/Private customers; hosted BAA depends on architecture and contract. We'll need Legal to look at scope.
[05:34] Liam Brooks: Any certifications around key management - FIPS?
[05:37] Ravi Singh: We can integrate with FIPS-validated HSMs in Private deployments; for hosted we use compliant KMS but may not expose FIPS attestation without private config.
[05:48] Ethan Cole: Competitors - we've been looking at Anthropic and SageMaker endpoints, main reasons are ease of model hosting and AWS-native VPC. How do you compare?
[05:57] Jamie Park: We're focused on inference economics and predictable latency; our Dedicated option mirrors many AWS networking features but with LLM-optimized runtime and caching to reduce cost. We can do a side-by-side for predicted token cost on your workload.
[06:10] Maya Torres: Ok let's map actionables - we'll need SOC2 report, an architecture doc for private, and a perf deep dive.
[06:17] Jamie Park: Noted. SE will prepare the diagrams and we'll send over compliance artifacts.
[06:22] Liam Brooks: One nit - in hosted mode do you ever surface raw request content in logs that are searchable? That's a no-go for us.
[06:29] Ravi Singh: In hosted logs we redact sensitive fields by default in search; raw request traces are stored but encrypted and access-limited. For PHI, Dedicated/Private prevents that exposure.
[06:41] Dr. Sarah Nguyen: Timeframe - we want pilot in ~6 weeks, must have legal and compliance sign-offs.
[06:47] Jamie Park: That's doable. We'll aim to get the docs over this week and propose pilot kickoff dates.
[06:52] Ethan Cole: For the pilot can you provide a cost estimate for a Dedicated single-tenant GPU pool sized for 50 qps?
[06:59] Ravi Singh: SE will run numbers once we get your token size and latency constraints; we'll ask for a sample payload and QPS numbers in follow-up.
[07:10] Maya Torres: On retention again - we use 7-day retention for dev and 30 days for prod, can you support different retention per environment?
[07:18] Jamie Park: Yes per-route or per-environment retention profiles are supported in Dedicated/Private; hosted can support via separate workspaces or retention flags.
[07:27] Liam Brooks: What about eDiscovery - can we pull a time-bounded slice of logs for audit?
[07:31] Ravi Singh: Yes exports of audit logs for a time range and filtered by user/model/route are supported and can be delivered in machine-readable format to your archive bucket.
[07:42] Dr. Sarah Nguyen: Any insights on drift monitoring and alerts tied to quality regressions? We need to detect if a model starts hallucinating more.
[07:50] Jamie Park: Redwood Optimize includes quality monitoring and regression alerts tied to prompt sets and evals. We can hook that into your alerting.
[07:59] Ethan Cole: Ok one follow-up - SAML attributes mapping, can we pass department/group claims into RBAC?
[08:04] Ravi Singh: Yes SAML/SCIM mappings can be configured to map IdP groups into Redwood roles; we have config templates for Okta and Azure.
[08:14] Maya Torres: Last security detail - incident response and breach notification timeline?
[08:18] Jamie Park: We have an incident response plan with 24/72 hour initial notification windows depending on severity; specifics are in our security pack. For Dedicated/Private enterprise customers we commit to contracted notification SLAs.
[08:31] Liam Brooks: Are there penetration test reports or ongoing vulnerability scanning?
[08:34] Ravi Singh: Yes - quarterly pentests and continuous vuln scanning; we can share executive summaries and remediation timelines.
[08:44] Ethan Cole: Thanks, this is super helpful. What's our follow-up cadence?
[08:48] Jamie Park: We'll send the SOC2 and KMS whitepaper by Monday, SE will send VPC/Private diagrams by Thursday, and we'll propose pilot dates for the week of June 1.
[08:58] Maya Torres: Sounds good. Also include a note about BAAs and legal contacts.
[09:03] Jamie Park: Will do; I'll include Legal contact. Thanks everyone.

[09:10] Meeting close and brief off-record chatter as participants drop off.

Notes about transcript quality: occasional mis-attributions, transcription shows some filler words and short transcription artifacts (e.g., 'uh', 'yeah'), some product names were slightly off in speech-to-text (e.g., 'Sage maker' instead of 'SageMaker').

- Ravi to prepare Private/Dedicated architecture diagrams and SSO/SCIM config notes by 2026-05-28.
- Veridian to provide sample payloads and QPS numbers to SE for pilot sizing by 2026-05-26.
- AE to send initial pilot pricing for Dedicated and Private by 2026-05-27.
